items.title: OBB-PBD: Extending Parallel Box Decoding to Oriented Bounding Boxes for Referring Expression Grounding in Aerial Imagery
items.summary: The study extends parallel box decoding to oriented bounding boxes via double-angle parameterization, validates it with control probes, and improves rotated IoU on aerial vehicle visual grounding.

items.title: RoboJev: An Open Vision-Language Judge for Robot Success Detection
items.summary: RoboJev-27B is an open-weight vision-language model that predicts robot manipulation success from video frames using LoRA fine-tuning, calibrated token readouts, and source-specific regularization, achieving high accuracy and generalization across labs and robots.

items.title: Evolving to Match Capabilities: Improving Harness Self-Evolution via Skill Adaptation
items.summary: Harness self-evolution improves LLM agents via skill adaptation guided by a meta-skill that reformulates guidance to match executor capabilities, boosting weak models without parameter updates.

items.title: Constrained Decoding: Harmful or Beneficial? Revisiting Its Impact on LLM Performance
items.summary: Constrained decoding does not inherently harm reasoning; its effects depend on constraint type, with validity and reasoning constraints often improving reliability and accuracy by removing invalid paths.

items.title: DialFork: Going Beyond Factuality to Evaluate Procedural Hallucination in Conversational Agents
items.summary: DialFork introduces a benchmark and flow-aware metrics to detect procedural hallucinations in conversational agents by measuring dialogue-level process deviation rather than content similarity.

items.title: Trust Mechanisms for Offline Generative AI at the Edge: A Connectivity-Regime Framework and an Empirical Study on a Raspberry Pi 5
items.summary: Local retrieval-augmented generation on edge devices using signed knowledge packs and output validators improves efficiency but remains vulnerable to poisoned updates and cannot guarantee evidence truth.

items.title: CausalAlign: Causal Alignment of Video Generation Models for Consistent Ego-Motion
items.summary: CausalAlign improves long-horizon camera ego-motion consistency in diffusion video generators by aligning internal representations to 3D dynamics via delta-token space.

items.title: AV-FABLE: Audio-Visual Manipulation Forensics in Long-Form Videos
items.summary: AV-FABLE introduces a long-form audio-visual benchmark for sparse manipulations, showing that frozen perception features of audio-visual large language models contain forensic evidence best recovered via separate temporal decoders rather than language outputs.

items.title: Joint or Per-Option? Compact Encoders for Closed-Set Decisions from 17 Million to 1 Billion Parameters
items.summary: Many language-model pipelines end in a closed-set decision, such as selecting a tool. Prompting a large language model for it is slow and order-sensitive. We ask how small an encoder for such decisions can be and whether it should read the options jointly or separately. In a three-seed study at 32 million parameters, per-option scoring beats joint scoring on a held-out sample of a 37-benchmark decision suite by 5.8 points of chance-corrected skill at matched optimizer steps and by 2.8 at approximately matched training compute; two external benchmarks agree, though not significantly on their unseen tasks. Crossing reader with initialisation shows that the advantage requires a reranker initialisation, whose query-candidate pair input matches per-option reading; from the raw encoder the two readers are indistinguishable. Per-option scoring needs 5 to 13 times more encoder passes: at most twice the median latency, but more than four times the mean. Of six released joint encoders (17 million to 1 billion parameters), the 68- and 150-million-parameter models exceed a 435-million-parameter DeBERTa-v3 zero-shot classifier by 4.9 and 5.9 accuracy points on 209 overlap-audited System1-Arena tasks and are at least on par with it on the 145 tasks unseen in training. The smallest answers a median request in 14 milliseconds on 16 processor threads, against 728 for the classifier. Reordering options changes 12 to 23% of the joint models' answers (per-option scoring: none). Up to 68 million parameters, they lead their size range on a public leaderboard's private, mainly in-distribution tests.

items.title: More Memory, Better Videos? A Controlled Study of Visual Memory in Long-Video Generation
items.summary: Visual memory improves historical consistency but can reduce current-story accuracy by reinforcing outdated appearances, showing that retrieval relevance alone does not prove memory utility.

items.title: RoboHarness: A Simple Harness Outperforms VLA and World Action Models
items.summary: RoboHarness enables LLM agents to perform embodied manipulation via a visual-geometric control interface, surpassing specialized vision-language-action models on robotics benchmarks.

items.title: Thinking-in-Bets at Test Time Reduces Sycophantic Revisions in LLM Agents
items.summary: Thinking-in-Bets improves agent reliability by having models record verified claims before receiving user feedback, reducing false reversals and unnecessary edits while maintaining accuracy.

items.title: Assessing the CAD Capabilities of General-Purpose AI Models: A Case Study of GPT-6 Astra
items.summary: GPT-6 Astra demonstrates partial capability across CAD workflows but remains limited by geometric validity, parametric dependencies, and assembly errors.

items.title: Beyond Benchmarks: Can Small Open-Weight Models Get Real Coding Work Done?
items.summary: Empirical studies of open-weight coding agents reveal that verified code success depends on serving setup, protocol design, and hidden behavioral checks rather than text coherence alone.

items.title: EmbodiedLab: Benchmarking Embodied Agents That Act to Know
items.summary: EmbodiedLab evaluates embodied agents that must physically interact with simulated laboratory apparatus to discover scientific principles through self-directed experimentation.

items.title: Rethinking Video Storage for AI Training: Breaking Cross-Frame Dependencies for Efficient Random Access
items.summary: Co-designed sparse decoding and dependency-decoupled encoding reduce video decode overhead for random AI training sampling by bounding reconstruction per target.

items.title: Nested Sparsity for Scalable Pretraining and Continual Learning
items.summary: Nestor introduces nested sparsity in attention to improve conditional computation over standard mixture-of-experts transformers, enhancing pretraining, long-context adaptation, and continual learning.

items.title: Mycelium: A Meta-Study of Hallucination Detection Across Provenance, Typology, and Granularities
items.summary: Hallucination detection is analyzed as a benchmark-conditioned measurement problem across provenance, typology, and granularity axes, with a proposed Span Coverage F1 metric to address span-level evaluation variability.

items.title: Humans in Space: Can MLLMs Construct Human-Centric Spatial Understanding via Active Exocentric Exploration?
items.summary: While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) excel at zero-shot reasoning, their spatial capabilities are primarily evaluated through static, passive observation. In complex, human-centric scenes, occlusion often hides crucial geometric evidence, and passive benchmarks force models to guess rather than recognize their own visual uncertainty. To bridge this gap, we introduce SATE-Bench, a novel interactive benchmark comprising 316 real-world scenes and 2,525 multi-turn QA pairs to evaluate visual self-awareness and active exocentric view-exploration. It combines a Passive multi-view control with an Active exploration setting, where models start from a severely occluded view and must iteratively query adjacent viewpoints until they gather enough evidence to fully ``sate'' the question, scored by a step-penalized efficiency reward. Evaluating state-of-the-art MLLMs reveals that they terminate exploration prematurely while reporting high confidence, and struggle with fine-grained 3D geometric tasks; matched-view controls further attribute the Active--Passive gap primarily to insufficient evidence acquisition. Moreover, fine-tuning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) shows that rewarding view-seeking increases active exploration but lowers overall accuracy, as models over-explore and fail to fuse expanding multi-view contexts across turns. These findings indicate that scaling passive multi-view perception does not intrinsically yield active spatial reasoning, highlighting the need for models that know where to look, how to integrate what they see, and when to stop. Code and data are available at https://gtc-gh.github.io/SATE-Bench/

items.title: S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning
items.summary: S3AC introduces a stabilized actor-critic training method with difficulty-aware prompt sampling to improve long reasoning in large language models without relying on grouped rollouts.

items.title: HiP3R: Hierarchical Pose Graphs for Long-Horizon 3D Reconstruction
items.summary: HiP3R uses a hierarchical pose graph to merge local video reconstructions into globally consistent camera trajectories and 3D geometry without retraining.

items.title: Skill^{infty}: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Skill Optimization
items.summary: Skill∞ enables recursive self-improvement by letting a meta agent optimize both task skills and its own meta-skill through a reusable, agent-led procedure, improving performance across diverse domains.

items.title: Spatial Audio Generation and Editing with Executable Plans and Self-Distilling Transfusion
items.summary: AMBIT is a unified framework that generates and edits first-order ambisonics audio by coupling autoregressive scene planning with rectified-flow rendering, using a specialized continuous VAE and on-policy self-distillation to preserve spatial structure and acoustic fidelity.

items.title: Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL
items.summary: FORK jointly optimizes recall and precision via rubric-driven necessity credits and factual grading to improve response quality and reduce verbosity in reinforcement learning.

items.title: Build, Don't Play: Self-Improving LLM Research Agents Develop a Hearthstone Battlegrounds AI That Rivals Top Players
items.summary: AutoTavern demonstrates that self-improving LLM research agents can autonomously build a faithful game simulator and train a reinforcement learning agent that surpasses top human players in Hearthstone Battlegrounds.

items.title: RynnVLA-Latent: Scaling Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models with 3D-Grounded Latent Actions
items.summary: RynnVLA-Latent leverages latent actions derived from diverse video to pretrain large vision-language-action policies, achieving high success across simulated and real-world robot benchmarks without embodiment-specific tuning.

items.title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges
items.summary: This survey defines recursive self-improvement and organizes trustworthy advancement requirements into improvement validity, constraint preservation, and oversight across recursive update stages.

items.title: miniTE: Diagnosing and Bridging the Execution Gap in Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: MiniTE enables stable low-bit reinforcement learning for large language models by aligning cross-engine numerical execution and accelerating native 4-bit computation.

items.title: DynaFlow: Learning Free-Form Multi-Agent Orchestration
items.summary: DynaFlow enables adaptive multi-agent collaboration by letting a main agent synthesize executable workflows that coordinate sub-agents through structured execution and verification.

items.title: Δτ-Bench: Pushing Agents Toward a Moving Capability
items.summary: Δτ-Bench evaluates agent adaptability to evolving tool ecosystems, and Steward improves sustained success through incremental skill maintenance and dynamic provisioning.

items.title: AgentProofBench: Benchmarking Reusable Verifiers for Web Agents
items.summary: AgentProofBench evaluates reusable web-agent verification by linking frozen acceptance rules to execution traces, establishing baseline measurements for program-gate correctness and reuse.

items.title: Novel or Not? PatEx-Gym: Agentic Prior-Art Search for Novelty Assessment in Patent Examination
items.summary: PatEx-Gym introduces a framework with benchmarks, synthetic trajectory data, and a compact agent to evaluate iterative prior-art search and patent examination.

items.title: ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: ProAS improves credit assignment in critic-free reinforcement learning for LLM agents by using a dynamic reference graph to mask unreasonable incentives and redistribute penalties asymmetrically, boosting success rates and convergence speed.

items.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
items.summary: The paper proposes a unified framework for work agents that integrates foundation models with runtime harnesses to execute complex digital tasks reliably, introducing dimensions of persistence and openness alongside capability families and evaluation metrics.

items.title: Qwen-Image-PE: Learning Visual Design for Text-to-Image Prompt Enhancement
items.summary: Qwen-Image-PE improves text-to-image prompts via two-stage training with caption-based reverse distillation and groupwise design rewards, scaling across data, model size, and information density.

items.title: Extreme Compression of Per-Layer Embeddings via Cross-Layer Latent Vector Quantization
items.summary: OPTIC achieves extreme compression of per-layer embeddings by using token-shared indexed codes and layer-specific affine decoders fitted to the output path, preserving most model performance at up to 1000x compression with minimal inference overhead.

items.title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
items.summary: StreamVibe introduces a benchmark, streaming vision-language model, and hierarchical memory harness to enable proactive, intent-aware interaction with implicit and evolving user goals.

items.title: Trajectory2Gym: Decision-Grounded Compositional Interaction Synthesis for Tool-Use Agents
items.summary: Trajectory2Gym improves tool-use training by constructing interactions with compositional coverage and decision grounding rather than collecting successful trajectories.

items.title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
items.summary: InteractiveWorld provides a verifiable simulation environment and benchmark to evaluate whether multimodal language models can reliably guide humans through physical tasks.

items.title: Principia: Test-Time Hypotheses to Principle Construction for Scientific Discovery
items.summary: Principia is an LLM-based framework that builds and iteratively refines scientific principles during inference to accelerate discovery across molecular and biological tasks.

items.title: World-in-Context: Interactive Video World Modeling with In-Context Conditioning
items.summary: World-in-Context unifies view, action, and camera controls via explicit tokens and interaction-aware positional encoding to improve interactive video generation and navigation.

items.title: Continual Learning Exam: Benchmarking Long-Horizon RSI and Experiential Learning in LLM Agents
items.summary: A new benchmark evaluates whether LLM agents improve through repeated professional tasks with feedback, revealing limited sustained learning in current frontier models.

items.title: Trial by Trace: Benchmarking AI Agent Harnesses for Reliability and Failure Attribution
items.summary: TraceTrial-Bench evaluates agent harness reliability across seven components using mechanism-oriented tasks, trajectory tracing, and failure attribution to compare harness designs and diagnose failures.

items.title: Steering Black-Box Large Language Model Agents with Pitfall Anticipation World Model
items.summary: PAWM selectively predicts multi-step failures to guide black-box LLM agents away from pitfalls, improving performance via supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement co-training.

items.title: WorldCast: World-Consistent Character Video Generation with Large-Angle Camera Control
items.summary: CLACT and WorldCast enable consistent character video generation under large-angle camera motions by combining 3D point-cloud guidance with geometry-aligned memory attention.

items.title: WORTH Benchmark: Evidence Discovery under Not-Fully-Cooperative Information -- A Two-Episode Pilot
items.summary: The WORTH Benchmark evaluates autonomous evidence discovery and reasoning in mystery narratives, revealing that models select clues and participants inconsistently due to narrative structure.

items.title: DiscoDemo: Discovering Efficient and Diverse Robot Demonstrations for Imitation Learning
items.summary: DiscoDemo uses reinforcement learning to generate diverse successful robot manipulation trajectories for training more robust visuomotor imitation policies.

items.title: Function-Space Temporal Self-Distillation for Policy Optimization
items.summary: Function-Space Policy Optimization improves reasoning and tool-use accuracy by combining temporal consolidation with privileged adaptation, reducing memory use and outperforming baselines.

items.title: How Much Feedback Is Needed to Break Template Protection? The Geometric Vulnerability of Biometric Authentication
items.summary: Biometric authentication leaks geometric information enabling precise template reconstruction from binary feedback, and diffusion priors reduce query costs significantly.

items.title: Kolab: Benchmarking Human-Agent Collaboration in Long-Horizon Workflows
items.summary: Kolab is a dataset of professional screen recordings that reveals frontier AI agents overestimate collaboration quality and fail to predict expert adoption of contributions in long-horizon workflows.
